1Lakeshore Loop

This is the easiest trail in the park and the one most people do first. It follows the north shore west from the lodge and loops back on the bench above the water, so you have the lake in view the whole way.

Status
Open
Distance
4.2 mi
Climb
200 ft
Time
2 hr
Start
Basin Lodge trailhead
Terrain
Packed dirt and gravel. Flat along the shore, with one short climb to the bench. Muddy in places.

Start at the lodge trailhead and take the path down past the dock, then turn west along the shore. The first stretch is flat and right at the edge of the water, with a few gravel beaches where you can get your feet wet.

At the far end the trail turns away from the water and climbs through the trees to the bench, a level shelf above the lake. Most of the 200 ft of climbing is on this one stretch, and it doesn't last long.

The bench brings you back east through cedar and fir, with the lake below you on the right, and comes out behind the lodge.

What to look for

Tracks
Easiest to find first thing in the morning, in the mud along the water. Deer and snowshoe hare are the usual ones. Check anything else against the track card.
The reflection
On calm mornings the lake is a mirror. The bench on the way back is the best place to see the far shore upside down in it.
Loons
Two pairs nest on the lake. Listen for them from the shore early in the morning and again around sunset.
The view from the bench
Looking south from the bench you can see right across to Cedar Flats on the far shore. Bring binoculars.

Before you go

  • Sign the trail register at the lodge trailhead, and sign out when you're back.
  • Bring water and a warm layer. It's cooler down by the water than it looks from the lodge.
  • Canoes and kayaks rent by the hour at the lodge dock, life jackets included, if you'd rather see the shore from the water.
